newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECHS WANT OPINION HEARD IN NATO-RUSSIA TALKS.
newsitem.headline: CZECHS WANT OPINION HEARD IN NATO-RUSSIA TALKS.

text.p: The Czech Republic said on Monday that it is actively injecting its opinion into the negotiations between Russia and NATO over Moscow's objections to expanding the alliance to former Soviet-bloc countries.

"We are active participants in this process. We are communicating with various sides which are taking part in this discussion about (NATO's) strategic partnership with Russia," Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec told a news conference.
"It is important that the alliance, in the course of these negotiations, knows our opinions," he added.

Zieleniec, speaking after a meeting with Czech ambassadors assigned to member countries of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO), said that setting up a long-term dialogue between NATO and Russia was "extremely important.

The Czechs, along with Poland, and Hungary are aspirants widely expected to be chosen to join the alliance at a July summit of member states in Madrid, but Moscow has been vehemently opposed to the expansion.
Zieleniec stressed that Prague sought to avoid another historic decision which is made "about us, without us" -- an often-used Czech phrase.

The comment refers to the 1938 agreement of European powers which ceded parts of the Czech lands to Nazi Germany, and the Yalta agreement between victorious powers in World War Two which put Czechoslovakia under Moscow's sphere of influence.
"If you speak of the period leading up to the Madrid conference, we want to be involved in the preparation of the agenda of this conference," Zieleniec said.
He said the NATO-Russia deal should have a "political climax" when U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin meet in Helsinki for a summit late next week.
